\section*{Key Terms and Definitions}

\textbf{Standard Form (Linear Programming)}: A linear programming problem expressed as maximizing $\mathbf{c}^T \mathbf{x}$ subject to $\mathbf{A} \mathbf{x} \le \mathbf{b}$ and $\mathbf{x} \ge \mathbf{0}$.<L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 1><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 2>

\textbf{Augmented Matrix}: A matrix formed by combining the constraint matrix $\mathbf{A}$ with the identity matrix $\mathbf{I}$ to represent the constraints in a linear programming problem after introducing slack variables. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 3><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 5><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 6><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 7>

\textbf{Simplex Iterates}: The sequence of solutions generated by the simplex method during its iterative process of improving the objective function value. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 2><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 3>

\textbf{Basic Variables ($\mathbf{x}_B$)}: A subset of variables in a linear programming problem that are set to non-zero values to determine a basic feasible solution.  The number of basic variables equals the number of constraints. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 4><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 5><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 6><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 7><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 8><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 9><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 12><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 13><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 15><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 18><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 19><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 20>

\textbf{Non-Basic Variables ($\mathbf{x}_N$)}: The remaining variables in a linear programming problem that are set to zero to determine a basic feasible solution. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 4><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 5><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 6><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 7><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 8><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 9><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 12><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 13><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 15><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 18><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 19><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 20>

\textbf{Simplex Tableau}: A tabular representation of the simplex method's matrix operations, showing the current values of the variables, objective function, and coefficients needed for updating the solution during iterations. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 10><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 11><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 12><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 13><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 15><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 17><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 18><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 19><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 20><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 21>

\textbf{Complementary Slackness}: A condition that relates the primal and dual variables in a linear programming problem, stating that at optimality, either a primal variable or its corresponding dual variable must be zero. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 14>

\textbf{Optimal Solution}: The solution to a linear programming problem that maximizes (or minimizes) the objective function while satisfying all constraints. <L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 16><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 20><L[2024-09-24-SimplexMatrix] 21>
